The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that took place on 19.08.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 19.08.2023 at about 9.45 a.m., when he was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JH-2713 near Ganesh U Turn, Mahalakshmi Metro Station,
West of Chord road, Bengaluru city, at that time, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-57- F-0496 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner, caused the accident and as a result, he sustained grievous injuries.

It is contended that, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to NU hospital for first aid, then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, thereafter he was shifted to KC hospital, wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is contended that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as driver and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as he was doing earlier and lost his income.
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0496.
Hence, the respondent being the owner/insurer of the offending bus is liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent has appeared through its learned counsel and filed objection statement.
5. The Respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
On other grounds prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-

REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.2 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 19.08.2023 at about 9.45 a.m., when he was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JH-2713 near Ganesh U Turn,
Mahalakshmi Metro Station, West of Chord road, Bengaluru city, at that time, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-57-F- 0496 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner, caused the accident and as a result, he sustained grievous injuries.
It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending bus driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, the petitioners prayed to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, spot mahazar,
sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of BMTC Bus.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.

Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Ganesh U Turn,
Mahalakshmi Metro Station, West of Chord road, Bengaluru city,at that time, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-57-F-0496 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazer and Sketch prepared at the time of spot mahazer.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 it reflects that injured was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JH-2713 near Ganesh U Turn and suddenly the offending BMTC Bus came in a negligent manner and without any signal take a U turn from the left side of the petitioner's vehicle and dashed against motorcycle and him.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of BMTC Bus had come in a normal speed by observing road as well as ongoing vehicle, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P6 was also filed as against the driver of the BMTC Bus.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 and 5 coupled with Ex.P.7 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and Shiva V vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26214720/

14. It has to be noted that, in the instant case, the Respondent who is insurer of the BMTC Bus has disputed the occurrence of this accident involving the insured BMTC Bus bearing No.
KA-57-F-0496.

The said insurer has taken contention that, on the date of alleged accident the injured was going in motorcycle, while he was so going high speed in overtaking the bus and dashed to bus and sustained injuries and in the police records it is mentioned that injured was proceeding on his way near Ganesha U turn the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0496 taken the U turn without indication and hit against the petitioner is utterly false made with an ulterior motivation of getting compensation and hence, this claim petition is liable to be dismissed.

In support of such defence,
the said insurer has adduced the evidence of RW1 namely Shaik Mehaboob, the Driver of the offending BMTC Bus.

The said RW1 has deposed reiterating the above facts that the injured was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner at high speed in overtaking the bus and dashed against the right side of the bus.
But in support of his version RW1 has not produced any document.
As per the police record and also evidence of the PW1 it clears that the driver of the Bus has suddenly taken U turn to right side without observing the left side moving vehicles.

Though,
there is absolutely no legally acceptable evidence adduced on record to believe that the injured riding his motorcycle in high speed in overtaking the bus and himself dashed to the bus and sustained injuries.

15. Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing to be elicited from his mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P5 coupled with Ex.P7.
These documents clearly demonstrated that there is negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0496 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0496.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
Petitioner in order to prove his disability, examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and they got marked Ex.
P16 to P21.
17. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was doing driver work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and to prove the same,
petitioner has not produced any documents.

In the absence of document of income,
the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.

Shiva V vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26214720/
5
The incident occurred during the year 2023.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- per month.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.3.
In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained left scapula fracture, left redial stylaid fracture with DRUJ injury with multiple soft tissue injuries.
He was treated conservatively.

On clinical examination conducted by him he found that petitioner's complains of pain in left shoulder and wrist difficulty to ablution lift weight over the head with left upper limb, and do routine work.
He has assessed permanent physical disability to the upper limb at 30% and whole body disability at 10%.

Further, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajaykumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows;
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).

The second step is Shiva V vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26214720/
6
to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.
By applying the said precedent to the present case the petitioner is facing difficulty in doing day today activities.
Petitioner has also sustained other injuries.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 35 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 19.08.2023.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P8 Driving licence as 15.02.1988, the petitioner was aged 35 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 35 is 16 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.1,19,340/- as per Ex.P11 and prescriptions at Ex.P12.

I have examined the medical bills and receipts, and it reflects that, out of the credit final bill of Rs.1,06,503/- issued by Prakriya Hospital, the said hospital has given discount of Rs.20,654/- and Rs.73,350/- was borne by the Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., and remaining amount of Rs.12,500/- was paid by the petitioner.
Therefore, out of the medical bills, after deducting Rs.73,350/- and adding up of Rs.12,500/- paid by the petitioner, he is entitled for Rs.58,490/-.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.58,490/- and he is entitled for the same.

20. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 12 days, and also took follow treatment as out patient.
Certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.12,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.48,000/- (16,000 X 3) under this head.

22. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 35 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.

ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 60% shall be released to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and remaining 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
Further, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajaykumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows;
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.
This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P8 Driving licence as 15.02.1988, the petitioner was aged 35 years at the time of accident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,07,200/-(Rs.16,000x12x16x10/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.
22. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 35 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.
